Headless rules were probed with the CLI and the API against throwaway homes. Evidence: this sitting's probes under runs/evidence/2026-09-21T05-18-16Z/ and the harness captures under 2026-09-21T05-33-54Z/ and 2026-09-21T05-37-40Z/.

The surface in front takes the pin - the prototype when it fully covers the app - and mid-fade the pin button is disabled with "Slide fully to the prototype or the app first" (harness embed-pin-filed-on-the-prototype, embed-pin-mid-fade-refused).

Three pins stood on the review page (n-0097, n-0107, n-0308); Done on n-0097 from the panel verified it and the pin was gone from the app surface at once while the other two stayed at the same coordinates, and the thread stayed reachable in All (probe F embed-settled-pins-leave). The ghosted copy was not measured separately.

Resting on a pin shows a daisy tooltip with the thread id, kind and status, then rule · screen · element, then the first line quoted, wholly on the surface with no title attribute (harness embed-pin-tooltip).

The form opens just below the spot (spot y 121, form top 139) and flips above it near the bottom (spot y 674, form top 464 with bottom 656 inside the 704 surface) (harness embed-form-below-the-spot, embed-form-above-near-the-bottom).

One form and one placeholder, the question tick turns the placeholder mark to ?, the controls wear pointer and text cursors, and Escape takes form and placeholder away while pin mode stays on (harness embed-form-*).

On a 1440 layout scaled to 0.597 the pin records surface coordinates (position 39,21 in a 1440x1179 viewport), and pins keep their surface spots across fit, 1440, fade and a resize (harness embed-pin-filed-on-a-scaled-surface, embed-pin-spot-survives-zoom).

The thread screen leads with the body in 12.5px text with the provenance on one 11px line above it (lines: 1) and the where-line under it; a 4-reply history scrolls inside the body (scrollHeight 1635 in 405) rather than growing the screen (harness embed-thread-provenance).

A PNG dropped on the pin form showed a thumbnail, the filed thread n-0340 carries attachments [{file: attachments/n-0340-1.png, name: probe-shot.png}], the thread screen shows it under the words at 133x80, and clicking opens it at 896x533 (probe F embed-picture-on-a-pin).

The actions are short verbs on one row (Waive · Reopen · Done); Waive asks for its reason only when pressed ("Waiving is recorded with a reason — write it above, then press again"); a verified thread offers Reply alone; Done under the declared identity verified n-0097 and its pin left the page (harness embed-thread-*, thread-terminal-verified; probe F settled-pins-leave).

`walkdown where` names each location with the sentence that says why it is there - config yours and registering nothing, the registry naming the project and who registered it, the spec and runs under the home it registered (probe A, and C3 where a hand-written row is set aside with its reason).
Running `walkdown where` and `walkdown status` against a fresh home left the registry and the home byte-identical before and after (probe A: checksums unchanged, no new files).

A `.walkdown` folder nobody registered is not consulted: status in a directory with a stray .walkdown answers "No blueprint here. Nothing registered in <registry> contains this directory" (probe A), and a hand-written registry row without `registered:` is set aside by where and refused by status and thread new (probe C3).

The hand-written row naming a symlink is set aside by `where` ("written by hand"), refused by status and thread new, and never served: a root server lists repo and pack only. Import through a symlink to the pack's home resolves to the real path and says it is already listed as `pack`, twice. Standing in the pack reaches the pack's row. The first attempt in probe C linked to the pack's .walkdown folder rather than its home and was rightly told nothing there declares a blueprint; the rerun is in probes-registry-import-via-link.txt.
A plain `walkdown init` left the repository tree without a .walkdown folder; the home went under the machine's walkdown home and the registry named it (probe A).
Threads, runs, evidence and drafts sit beside the spec under the home in every layout probed - default home, --commit spec and --commit all - and `where` reports them under the same home (probe A).

`init --commit spec` put the home under the repository's .walkdown with a .gitignore keeping runs, evidence and drafts out; `--commit all` the same with no ignore; re-running with --commit moved the home whole and the registry followed (probe A).
`walkdown skills` wrote the skills under the user's own skills directory by default and into the project only with --project, saying where each went (probe A).
A second `init` in the same project refused to make a second home and pointed at the one already registered; a second blueprint got its own numbered home (probe A).
`walkdown move` relocated the home to the path asked for, rewrote the registry row, and nothing moved on its own: a stray copy of the home elsewhere in the tree was never adopted (probe A).
On a repo with an AGENTS.md and no CLAUDE.md, init placed its block in AGENTS.md alone and created no CLAUDE.md; the block names where the blueprint is (probe C1).

A line of the person's own above the block and one below survived two more placings byte-identical (diff IDENTICAL, one walkdown:begin marker); after the spec moved (--commit none) the block was updated in place with the new path and the person's lines stayed (probe C2, C2b).

The judge prompt hands out a logical key `runs/evidence/<ts>/` and says which path this machine resolves it to, and tells the agent to cite the key never the path (probe D3); the evidence modal on the real board lists files by that key and resolves them to pictures and text (probe G).

A run recorded on one machine reads on another without the record being edited: git_sha carries a -dirty suffix as provenance and spec_hash says what was judged, and the clone in probe D7 read the 515 inherited runs and reported them (probe A, D7).
Lint reports a rule with no steps as an error: "rule has no steps — given/when/then is what a check gets built from, and a statement alone leaves it to be invented" (probe C5).

An agent reply chaining three thoughts with dashes was refused by the voice gate, landed with --as-is, and the same words from a person landed unchallenged (probe B6).
